pr_title: Prune low-level ASN.1 parse errors from error queue in decoder_process()
pr_body:
It turns out that while loading credential files such as `test/certs/root-cert.pem` 
spurious error queue entries are produced such as
```
C02727C5197F0000:error::asn1 encoding routines:(unknown function):header too long:crypto/asn1/asn1_lib.c:103:
```
This is strongly related to #12645.
pr_comments: This looks okay to me, I'm not sure of the ramifications so I'll defer to @levitte
It breaks current tests but fixes #12838
It also partly fixes #12840.

Whoaaa, that's a bit over generalised, isn't it? This essentially means that really really anything that informs the user of something breaking in a bad way in the provider is just thrown away. That's a bit of an over-shoot.

I'm not entirely sure what's the right answer here. Libcrypto can't make assumptions on what errors are recorded. It could simply be that the implementation drops certain specific ones, such as the asn1 stuff, which is appropriate since they do guesswork....

Good point, so I'll restrict this to ASN.1 errors (similarly to #12645).
I'm currently investigating on the two test failures..

> Good point, so I'll restrict this to ASN.1 errors (similarly to #12645).
> I'm currently investigating on the two test failures..

I experimented with the storeutl, x509, and pkcs12 app and found that is (likely) sufficient to suppress only `ASN1_R_HEADER_TOO_LONG`.
Doing so, also the two sub-tests in `30-test_evp.t` that failed before now pass again.

For example, 
```
apps/openssl x509 -in test/certs/v3-certs-RC2.p12 -passin pass:v3-certs
```
no more outputs the misleading error
```
C0975086D97F0000:error::asn1 encoding routines:(unknown function):header too long:crypto/asn1/asn1_lib.c:103:
```
Tomorrow I 'll recheck your patch against #12838

Phew, it was a pretty hard job to sort out junk error queue entries such that only the relevant one(s) remain.
This PR now fully solves #12840.
Note that I also hat to (re-)introduce error queue printing on fatal errors in `load_key_certs_crls()` of `apps.c`.
I was too quick with the approval - the Travis failure is relevant. Missing #ifdef conditional on disabled EC.

Thanks @paulidale and @t8m for your comments.

The error reporting business in general is unfortunately rather ad-hoc.

And various functions like `asn1_d2i_read_bio()` are still too brutal simply clearing all the error queue - 
they should use `ERR_set_mark()` and when needed clear only those entries they are responsible for.

> I was too quick with the approval - the Travis failure is relevant. Missing #ifdef conditional on disabled EC.

I think I've meanwhile found a solution that is more elegant also in other respects.
On this occasion I've cleaned up the diagnostic strings on credentials loading failure in many apps.
I confirm that it still fixes #12838

I'd like to add regression tests that no low-level ASN.1 parsing errors are thrown/shown by
```
apps/openssl x509 -noout -passin pass:v3-certs -in test/certs/v3-certs-RC2.p12
```
nor by
```
 apps/openssl x509  -in test/certs/root-cert.pem -out non-existent-dir/
```

How best to do that?
For simplicity I'd like to do to this at scripting level, e.g., in `test/recipes/90-test_store.t`.
Is there a system-independent way of getting hold of the `stderr` output?

>  Is there a system-independent way of getting hold of the `stderr` output?

Hmm, for these kinds of tests it will be sufficient to do them on Linux-like systems, so something like this should work:
```
apps/openssl x509 -in test/certs/root-cert.pem -out non-existent-dir/ 2>&1 | grep asn1
```

> Is there a system-independent way of getting hold of the `stderr` output?

OpenSSL test module comes with a manual:

```
perldoc -o man util/perl/OpenSSL/Test.pm
```

I believe you're looking for the extra arguments you can give the `cmd`, `app` and `test` functions

> I confirm that it still fixes #12838

@beldmit, does this still hold using the current alternative solution?
The current patch still works for me.

> I believe you're looking for the extra arguments you can give the `cmd`, `app` and `test` functions

Thanks @levitte for this helpful hint. 
On this occasion I've extended the documentation of `Test.pm` with some clarifications.
Using it, I've been able to add regression tests for the error queue pruning and for a to-the-point error output for PKCS#12 input with (meanwhile by default) unsupported RC2-40-CBC.
Still works for me :)

Also here meanwhile all tests pass. 
Ping for re-approval.
Still works for me.

> Err, what made you sprinkle err marking stuff in `try_key_value_legacy`?

They turned out to be needed there analogously to the ones you sprinkled in `ossl_store_handle_load_result()`.
As mentioned above https://github.com/openssl/openssl/pull/12893#discussion_r491734635 otherwise those spurious parse errors still would show up in the 'minimal' configuration done as part of the Travis CI:
`--strict-warnings no-shared no-dso no-pic no-aria no-async no-autoload-config no-blake2 no-bf no-camellia no-cast no-chacha no-cmac no-cms no-cmp no-comp no-ct no-des no-dgram no-dh no-dsa no-dtls no-ec2m no-engine no-filenames no-gost no-idea no-ktls no-mdc2 no-md4 no-multiblock no-nextprotoneg no-ocsp no-ocb no-poly1305 no-psk no-rc2 no-rc4 no-rmd160 no-seed no-siphash no-siv no-sm2 no-sm3 no-sm4 no-srp no-srtp no-ssl3 no-ssl3-method no-ts no-ui-console no-whirlpool no-asm`.

As I commented earlier https://github.com/openssl/openssl/pull/12893#discussion_r490837242, 
not doing the pruning centrally (for instance in `decoder_process()`), one needs to detect and manipulate basically all spots where a decoding attempt is done. As expected this is a PITA. Meanwhile I've spent around two work days on it.

> As expected this is a PITA. Meanwhile I've spent around two work days on it.

I still think it's worth it, and I'm glad you do.  The sledgehammer approach that you had earlier is quicker in the moment, but dodgy, and it's too likely that we'd get issues with lost important errors and would have to do what you just did anyway.

This exercise has me wish there was a general mechanism to filter errors.  A hook in the error reporting code, so one could decide programmatically that certain errors will simply not be added to the error queue.  *That* is something `OSSL_DECODER_from_bio()` could "install" before the `decoder_process()` call, and "uninstall" after that call returns.

> This exercise has me wish there was a general mechanism to filter errors. A hook in the error reporting code, so one could decide programmatically that certain errors will simply not be added to the error queue. _That_ is something `OSSL_DECODER_from_bio()` could "install" before the `decoder_process()` call, and "uninstall" after that call returns.

Yes, something in that direction would be nice. 
The filtering could be at least be according to the (sub-)library/module identifier,
and it would be good to add a severity level as well (as presumably discussed already at several places).
Still approved by me

24 hours has passed since 'approval: done' was set, but as this PR has been updated in that time the label 'approval: ready to merge' is not being automatically set.  Please review the updates and set the label manually.
Merged - thanks!

issue_context.body:
Command line:
```
./openssl_wrap.sh ocsp -issuer cacert.pem -CAfile cacert.pem -cert cert.pem -signer cert.pem -signkey seckey.pem -reqout request2.der
```

Result:
```
00F19516BD7F0000:error::asn1 encoding routines:ASN1_get_object:header too long:crypto/asn1/asn1_lib.c:105:
```

The openssl_wrap.sh script:
```
#!/bin/bash
  
OPENSSLDIR=`pwd`/../openssl
export LD_LIBRARY_PATH=$OPENSSLDIR
OPENSSL_CONF=`pwd`/engine.conf $GDB $OPENSSLDIR/apps/openssl $@
```

engine.conf file:
```
openssl_conf = openssl_def
[openssl_def]
engines = engine_section

[engine_section]

[gost_section]

dynamic_path = /path/to/gost.so
```

comments: The bug was introduced recently, #12740 fixed all the issues present at that moment.
As the `request.der` is created, it seems to be just a lack of popping stack errors in some cases.
If I understand correctly, the last time when the error is put into the stack happens on loading a signer key. Don't understand, BTW, when it should be cleared from the stack
This is going to be fixed by #12893

review_comments: How do you know there's nothing to load before you tried to load?

Because the called did not provide any result pointer, so the loading request is effectively void.
That's why I prepended this with "Internal error:".
The message is still misleading.  "nothing to load into from %s" might be better
Why is it a bad idea to include the description here?
Oh, now i see the elaborate stuff after `end:`...  Never mind
The common parts of description etc. are added, once and for all error cases, in the `end:` section of the function body.
